Hi Ben,

I hope you’re well. I lead the Computational Linguistics Lab at Midwest University. We’ve been evaluating Redwood through the PLG signup and a few grad students have been experimenting with the hosted API. The department is a nonprofit educational unit and we’d like to run a larger-scale pilot for 3 months to evaluate reproducibility in our coursework and several research pipelines.

Can Redwood provide academic trial credits (or a promo code) that we can distribute to ~12 student accounts and two lab service accounts? We’ll primarily use the embeddings and chat endpoints; estimated usage is ~500k tokens/month.

I’ve attached a short sponsor letter from the department and a CSV of course IDs. Happy to provide any other paperwork needed.

Best,
Laura

Hi Laura — nice to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the sponsor letter. A couple quick items we need to finalize: 

- Confirmation of nonprofit status: does Midwest University have a specific registration or tax ID number we should reference? A departmental letter on official letterhead (we have one attached) usually suffices.
- Intended billing owner: is there a university PO contact if you expect to convert to paid after pilot?
- Data handling: we will provide a free credits pool under our standard PLG academic terms; if you need any additional contractual terms (DPA or KMS requirements) please flag now.

Provision recommendation for your usage: for a 3-month pilot at 500k tokens/month we typically allocate a $3,000 credit pool (this is conservative and can be adjusted after a week of telemetry). That covers embeddings + chat at standard PLG rates. If everyone will use higher-context sequences let us know and we’ll increase accordingly.

If that sounds good, I’ll authorize issuing a promo code and the console link to spin up scoped API keys.
